label: D2 update gate set by this trial choice x reached state: low after a1, highest a2->S2
terms: (phase == D2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 2) * (state == 2) ;; (phase == D2) * choice
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 32 sits near 1 at D1 and GO (residuals there < 0.02) and drops at D2 (mean ~0.7); all magnitude beyond timing is at D2 and is set by the choice just made and the state just reached (both observed at D2). Relative to timing: a1->S1 about -0.33, a1->S2 -0.14, a2->S1 +0.20, a2->S2 +0.26 (so z is lowest, i.e. strongest hidden-state rewrite, after a1 common, and close to 1 after a2). Within cells, the model policy logit at D2 (choice, more a1-leaning = lower z) adds graded variation. The 4 observed-only choice x state terms alone give test R^2 beyond timing 0.91 (dev 0.914); adding the policy term gives dev 0.96. Previous-trial history (prev action, prev reward x state) adds < 0.01; value, future reward and hidden good state are not needed (good-state and last-trial reference tables mostly proxy the current choice). Ceiling all = 0.98.

issues: Minor overclaim: 'previous-trial history adds less than 0.01'. Adding (phase==D2)*last_is('a1 S2 r'), last_is('a2 S2 u') and last_is('a1 S1 u') to the 5 terms raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.957 to 0.973 (+0.016). A single MB-switch term (phase==D2)*(prev_action>0)*(prev_common != prev_reward) gives 0.967, and with an extra x(action==1) term 0.973.

Systematic miss with the original terms: at D2 after an 'a1 S2 r' (rare-rewarded) trial, z is under-predicted by a mean of +0.139. Smaller under-predictions at D2 follow a2 S2 u (+0.053) and a1 S1 u (+0.048). All three are trials after which a model-based agent should switch, and z at D2 is higher after them. Fitted weights: +0.15, +0.08, +0.07. Adding these terms brings the remaining misses-by-history to |err| <= 0.02.

Checks that held up: the residual table by choice x state at D2 matches the stated values (-0.335 / -0.137 / +0.200 / +0.257). The 4 observed-only cell terms give test 0.909 and adding the policy term gives 0.957. The choice weight is negative, so a more a1-leaning policy logit does mean lower z. D1 and GO residuals are under 0.02. An invalid-trial term (action==0) adds nothing (0.9574). The 'policy logit' term is a model output, not a future variable, so 'uses future variables: false' is correct.
